name: Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)
description: Regulation (EU) 2024/2847 (Cyber Resilience Act), OJ L, 2024/2847, 20.11.2024. Applies from 11 December 2027 (Article 71(2)); Article 14 from 11 September 2026 and Chapter IV (Articles 35 to 51) from 11 June 2026 (Article 71(2), second subparagraph). Citations are anchored by catalogue/anchor-test.sh. Scope caveat: the CRA binds manufacturers placing a product with digital elements on the Union market, not operators of a running workload, so this pack evidences product properties an agent manifest happens to assert, never conformity.

applicability.note: Article 71(2), first subparagraph: 'This Regulation shall apply from 11 December 2027.' Read verbatim from the EUR-Lex primary text. The second subparagraph carves out two earlier dates -- Article 14 from 11 September 2026 and Chapter IV (Articles 35 to 51) from 11 June 2026 -- so this framework-level window is correct ONLY for the Annex I essential requirements. Every check this pack currently ships evidences an Annex I requirement (Part I point (2)(b), Part II point (1), Part II point (7) and Part I point (2)(f)), so none of them is governed by either carve-out and the framework window is the right level today. The moment an Article 14 reporting check or a Chapter IV conformity-assessment check is added it MUST carry its own check-level or controlSet-level window, because a flat 11 December 2027 would over-gate it by 15 and 18 months respectively. Note the carve-outs sit in the second subparagraph of Article 71(2), not in a separate Article 71(3).

controlSets.name: CRA: Security by Design and Default
controlSets.description: Essential cybersecurity requirements relating to the properties of products with digital elements. Part I point (2) is conditioned on the cybersecurity risk assessment of Article 13(2) and applies only 'where applicable', so a flat fail is stricter than the obligation in a way no scanner can adjudicate. CITES: Annex I Part I; Article 13

controls.name: CRA-1.1 Security by Default Configuration
controls.description: Annex I Part I point (2)(b) requires a product to be made available 'with a secure by default configuration ... including the possibility to reset the product to its original state'. This control evidences only the first limb; the reset capability is not evidenced. CITES: Annex I Part I point (2)(b)

checks.name: Secure-by-default runtime profile
checks.description: Ensures system components ship and run with hardened security configurations by default.
checks.remediation: Enable default hardened security profile in agent manifest.

controlSets.name: CRA: Vulnerability Handling and SBOM
controlSets.description: Vulnerability handling requirements borne by the manufacturer under Article 13(8). CITES: Annex I Part II; Article 13

controls.name: CRA-2.1 Verified SBOM and Vulnerability Management
controls.description: Annex I Part II point (1) requires identifying and documenting vulnerabilities and components 'including by drawing up a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at the very least the top-level dependencies'. The CRA mandates no specific format: Article 13(24) empowers the Commission to specify format and elements by implementing act, and none is in force, so the CycloneDX/SPDX allow-list is this pack's choice and not the obligation. The CRA requires no SBOM verification at all, and top-level dependency coverage is not evidenced. CITES: Annex I Part II point (1); Article 13(24)

checks.name: Verified Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
checks.description: Requires the agent manifest to declare an SBOM in CycloneDX or SPDX format and to assert that it was verified. The SBOM itself is never parsed and its dependency coverage is never inspected: 'verified' is a self-asserted boolean, not a checked provenance claim.
checks.celExpression: has(agent.sbom) && type(agent.sbom) == map && has(agent.sbom.format) && (agent.sbom.format == 'CycloneDX' || agent.sbom.format == 'SPDX') && has(agent.sbom.verified) && agent.sbom.verified == true
checks.remediation: Attach signed CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM metadata to agent workload.

controlSets.name: CRA: Software Integrity and Updates
controlSets.description: Integrity of a product's data, commands and configuration, and the secure distribution of security updates. CITES: Annex I Part I point (2)(f); Annex I Part II point (7)

controls.name: CRA-3.1 Cryptographic Integrity and Signed Updates
controls.description: Annex I Part II point (7) requires 'mechanisms to securely distribute updates ... to ensure that vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated in a timely manner', and Annex I Part I point (2)(f) requires protecting integrity against unauthorised modification. SLSA is named nowhere in the CRA: a build-provenance level is a proxy for the secure distribution obligation, not evidence of it, and this control verifies neither a signature nor an update mechanism. CITES: Annex I Part II point (7); Annex I Part I point (2)(f)

checks.name: Cryptographically signed software provenance
checks.description: Reads the SLSA build level the agent manifest asserts and requires it to be exactly SLSA_LEVEL_3. No signature is verified and no cosign material is inspected: this is a self-asserted label, not an attestation.
checks.remediation: Build and sign artifacts satisfying SLSA Level 3 provenance criteria.
